Case: Patient D is a 55-year-old Black woman presenting with 9 months of progressive low-back and leg pain. Patient D states that her pain is worse after prolonged ambulation and radiates to her right buttock and thigh. Patient D has tried physical therapy and conservative pain medications including epidural steroid injections and NSAIDs. On physical exam, you observe that her pain is significantly worse with a right straight-leg raise and there are no focal deficits. MRI of the lumbar spine reveals grade-2 spondylolisthesis at L4-L5 with degenerative changes contributing to severe canal and neuroforaminal stenosis. Flexion-extension X rays show dynamic instability of L4 on L5.
Question: Would you offer hydrocodone to Patient D? Yes or No? If yes, how much supply would you give – Low (1 week), or High (4 weeks) supply? Explain.
